the scoring elevates a strict 0.01pp win-rate-accuracy gate

(null when default mode).

the pack name carries an X% tag AND the caller didn't pin a custom winRate,
tagged-mode triggers. ApplyStagedRetuneResult.priceSearch carries the new

band is covered for any reasonable pack price (default mode stays at 50).

entries.subject: Pack history: clickable rows with per-card odds + DIFF-vs-current overlay

Closed: the existing header (pack, action chip, price, risk summary,

LIVE pool (owner-gated server action getLivePackPoolForDiff) and
overlays per-card deltas: added since (rose), removed since (emerald),
weight changed (amber), plus a 'Live %' column alongside 'Snapshot %'.

entries.subject: Pack retune review: one-click "+ Add a card in $X-$Y range" from infeasibility errors
entries.body:
When the retune review (or pool editor) flags a pack infeasible with an
explicit price band ("Add a card priced between $1.25 and $6.25"), the owner
had to open the Builder, filter to that range, and add a card by hand. This
turns the suggestion into a one-click action.

risk.ts: `ShapeWeightsLimit` gains an optional `suggestedRange` carrying the
explicit USD band derived from the limit. Attached at the four range-emitting
limit sites: `no-win-cards` (cap-filtered → [price, maxWinCap]; intrinsic →
[price, 5*price]), `no-win-band-card` ([price, 5*price]), `ev-out-of-range`
(too-low → [0, 0.5*price]; too-high → [price, 5*price]), and `no-dust-cards`
([0, 0.5*price]).

builder-card-picker.tsx: accepts optional controlled-open (`open` /
`onOpenChange`) plus `initialPriceMin` / `initialPriceMax` seeds. The seeds
re-apply on every open transition so re-opening with a new range resets the
filter; uncontrolled mode + the existing call site stay unchanged.

pool-editor.tsx: forwards `pickerOpen` / `onPickerOpenChange` /
`pickerInitialPriceMin/Max` through to the embedded BuilderCardPicker. The
parent now drives the picker programmatically.

review-card.tsx: when `limit.suggestedRange` is set, renders a house-emerald
"+ Add a card in $X-$Y range" button beneath the existing band-aware error.
One click opens the inline pool editor (if not already open) AND the picker
pre-filtered to the suggested band. The legacy "Edit pool / add a card >=
price" fallback still shows for limit kinds without a range (degenerate-pool,
empty-pool, no-dust-mass, edge-unreachable, etc.).

entries.subject: Pack retune inline editor: addCard renormalises so KPI preview shifts visibly
entries.body:
Adding a card with hard-coded odds:1 next to existing rows summing to ~100%
gave the new card ~1% of the share — KPIs barely budged and the owner
thought the live preview was frozen. Now addCard allocates the new card a
fair 100/N share and scales the existing rows by (N-1)/N so the total stays
at exactly 100%. House edge / EV / Win rate / Max win / Tier all jump
meaningfully when a high-value card is added, the OddsTotalChip stays green,
and adding a card priced >= price flips a no-win pack feasible immediately
(banner clears + Auto-tune & push enables).

entries.subject: Pack retune: price-search lever (owner-opt-in ±25% for cleaner odds)
entries.body:
searchBestPriceForCleanSnap wraps shapeWeights to sweep cent-stepped
candidate prices around the staged price (default ±25%, max 50
candidates) and pick the one that lands every card on a clean ladder
rung. applyStagedPackEditAndRetune accepts allowPriceSearch via the
targets param; when true the chosen price is written to packs.price and
the audit event records the price_search_* trace. Pool editor exposes a
default-OFF checkbox the owner ticks to opt in; the confirm gate shows a
"server may adjust price" note, and the post-write toast surfaces the
chosen price when it deviates from the base. Two new harness checks pin
the wrapper's contract (snap-prefer, base-prefer-when-clean,
degradation-aware fellBackToBase) — all 42 risk checks pass.

entries.subject: Pack retune review: sort inline pool editor by card price desc
entries.body:
The inline card-pool editor (Bulk Re-tune review) was appending newly
added cards to the bottom of the table regardless of value, so a $0.72
add could land BELOW a $0.08 dust card. The owner now always sees the
pool ordered most-expensive-first.

Adds a stable `sortByPriceDesc` helper and applies it to both the
initial seed (replaces the old `order` sort) and to `addCard`, so a
fresh pick lands in its price-sorted slot (e.g. between a $810 jackpot
and a $0.08 dust card). Manual DnD via `onReorder` still wins so the
owner can hand-place same-priced variants. Stable sort preserves
insertion order on ties.

The Approve handlers rewrite `order: i` from the (now sorted) row
index, so display order = write order = sorted-by-price order.

entries.subject: Pack retune snap: within-band monotonicity + strict GRAIL top rarity
entries.body:
Owner-facing designer invariants — the snap was producing zigzags and ties
that read wrong to a human pack designer (e.g. $810 and $508 both at 0.05%,
$118→0.10% then $114→0.075% then $75→0.10%).

Adds `repairSnapMonotonicity` post-process applied after both the basic
buffer-residual snap and the local-search refinement:

  1. Within each band (GRAIL, WIN, NEARMISS, DUST), as card value descends,
     probability must NON-DECREASE.
  2. STRICT rarity at GRAIL top: the most-expensive grail card lands at a
     strictly lower ladder rung than the second-most-expensive.

Walks each band cheapest→most-expensive, demoting violators to the
next-lower clean ladder rung. Recomputes buffer residual to keep total at
100%. If demotion would push a card below the smallest rung, repair fails
and the caller falls back to precise weights (existing safety contract —
never regresses).

Harness sweep acceptance threshold lowered from 20% → 5% (monotonicity is
strictly tighter than the prior snap; rejects more candidates by design).
All 40 risk checks pass.

entries.subject: Pack retune lottery skew: steep grail-band redistribution for tagged 1%/5% packs
entries.body:
Auto-retune (shapeWeights) lands a near-flat WITHIN-grail distribution for
tagged lottery packs — the $810 jackpot fires ~4× as often as the $60 grail
for a $1.25 "1% 18 PLUS" pack. Owners hand-tune lottery distributions with a
~190× ratio (cheapest grail dominates) so short-term variance stays bounded.

New post-process applyLotterySkew (insights/edge-calc/risk.ts) re-shapes the
GRAIL band along value^(-β) (β=2) AFTER the solver and BEFORE the clean-snap
step. Two phases:
1. Redistribute grail mass: value^(-β=2) gives ratio (60/810)^-2 ≈ 181× —
   matching owner verbatim ~190×.
2. EV-compensate by scaling dust weights down via bisection until edge lands
   back at target. Within-grail ratio preserved; win-rate drifts slightly
   upward (~1% target lands at ~1.6% for the spec's pool — inside the
   existing 2pp tolerance).

Trigger gate: targetWinRate ≤ 0.05 (1%/5% packs). Normal packs are byte-for-
byte unchanged (no-op). New lotterySkewApplied flag on ShapeWeightsSuccess
so callers can surface "lottery-skewed distribution" in reviews/changelogs.

Test harness extended with two new checks:
- 5% tagged close-range-grails pool: skew applied, value^(-2) ratio holds.
- The real "1% 18 PLUS" pool: $810 at 0.002%, $60 at 0.36%, ratio 182×,
  edge 10.99% (target). Matches owner verbatim.
- Normal 20%-win pack: lotterySkewApplied=false (no-op preserved).
- Full sweep (11304 feasible / 5112 infeasible combos) still green.

Gates: tsc + lint + npm run build (exit 0).

entries.subject: Pack retune snap: buffer-residual ladder snap + local-search refinement
entries.body:
Replaces the naive "snap-then-renormalize" snap with a buffer-residual scheme
plus a 3-stage escalating local search. N-1 cards land on EXACT ladder rungs
(0.05%, 0.1%, 10%, 25%, ...) and one buffer card (argmax mass, typically the
dust) absorbs the residual so the total stays at 100% without re-normalizing
every rung (which is what produced the ugly 0.0521% the prior version
generated for the owner's "1% 18 PLUS" pool).

Acceptance is tiered: basic snap → 3^5 local search → 5^4 search → 3^7 search.
The first stage that lands edge within ±0.05pp of target AND preserves
win-rate within tol is accepted; otherwise the precise weights are kept
(safety fallback — the snap never regresses edge).

Snap-acceptance on the existing sweep grid: 0.15% → 27.5% (and the "1% 18
PLUS" pool now produces clean numbers: 10/11 cards on exact ladder rungs).

Updates the existing harness (#14) to cover the new contract:
  • (a) normal-edge $5 pack lands 85% / 10% / 5% on ladder
  • (b) "1% 18 PLUS" lottery pool snaps via local search to clean rungs
  • (c) safety contract holds even when fallback kicks in
  • (d) sweep acceptance ≥ 20% (regression floor)
  • (e) snap primitive: N-1 entries on exact ladder rungs

entries.subject: Pack retune review: server-shaped Auto-tune & push (safe edit path)
entries.body:
Inline pool editor now has a primary "Auto-tune & push to production" button
next to the existing "Approve edited pool" (demoted to outline + tooltip
warning). The new path sends only the staged pool IDENTITY (cards + order +
color/animation + optional new price) — the server picks the weights via
shapeWeights against the pack's auto-targets so bad weights can't land on
prod from this entry point.

New server action applyStagedPackEditAndRetune (retune-actions.ts) mirrors
applyPackRetune's paranoia (owner gate + retune token + capability + scope)
PLUS applyPackEdit's real-card identity check (cards.findMany), runs
shapeWeights server-side with FAIL-CLOSED asserts (edge ≥ target, max-win ≤
cap, |winRate − target| ≤ tol, EDIT_EDGE_FLOOR backstop), captures an "edit"
snapshot, writes via the same delete-then-createMany pack_cards transaction,
audits pack_edited_and_retuned with before/after risk + auto-target flags,
and refreshes the ADMIN risk row.

EditApprovePayload becomes a discriminated union (mode: "verbatim" |
"auto-tune"); PendingWrite gets a new "edit-and-retune" kind that routes
through the same two-step confirm gate (step 1 + final hard confirm copy
adapt for the auto-tune variant). 2FA token + token-expiry retry path
shared unchanged across all three writes.

entries.subject: Pack retune/edit: server-side fail-closed edge floor (5%)
entries.body:
applyPackEdit (the verbatim-weights MAIN write path used by the retune
review's "Approve edited pool" action) previously accepted ANY weights
the operator approved. The client-side double-confirm gate is a UX
defense and was demonstrably bypassed once by a stale browser bundle.

This adds a server-side hard floor: the action re-computes the edited
pool's risk with the existing computePackRisk call, and if the resulting
edge < EDIT_EDGE_FLOOR (5%) it throws BEFORE capturePackSnapshot and
BEFORE the pack_cards transaction — so no low-edge pool can reach MAIN
no matter what client state was. The refusal is audited best-effort as
"pack_edit_refused_edge_floor" with the attempted edge / max-win.

Belt-and-suspenders: the same floor check is added at the end of
applyPackRetune's existing fail-closed asserts. shapeWeights already
fails closed below targetEdge (which is itself clamped to the
edge-curve floor), so this is cheap insurance for a future refactor.

EDIT_EDGE_FLOOR lives in pack-studio/_lib/risk-config.ts (single source
of truth, alongside the other thresholds). 5% is intentionally generous
vs. the 10.99% edge-curve target — the curve is the TARGET, this is the
absolute "never ship below this" guard rail. Owner can lift it in a
follow-up.

Gates: tsc clean, lint clean, next build exit 0.

Browser-verification on /pack-studio/retune (attempting a low-edge edit
should show the new error message) is PENDING — server logic verified
by build gates only.

entries.subject: Pack retune snap: round odds to clean ladder + safety fallback
entries.body:
The auto-retune solver produces edge-correct weights whose percentages
read as ugly decimals (0.0132% / 0.0173% / 0.0205%). This adds a post-
process that snaps each card's probability to the nearest value on a
fixed ladder of round numbers (1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 7.5, 10, ...
across decades 1e-6% to 100%), re-normalizes, and quantizes back to
integer weights — only KEEPING the snapped result when edge stays
within +/-0.05pp of target AND >= target (one-sided-up invariant).
Otherwise falls back to the precise weights. Algorithm guarantees no
edge regression.

- New export `snapWeightsToCleanLadder` (pure, dep-free).
- New `snapped?: boolean` field on `ShapeWeightsSuccess`.
- Integrated as the LAST step inside `shapeWeights` — band logic, EV
  solver, cap pre-filter, target-edge curve, fail-closed asserts all
  untouched.
- Two new harness tests: a snap-accept pool (small bimodal) + the
  '1% 18 PLUS' pool where the snap would crash edge (verifies the
  safety fallback). Harness now prints both the would-be snapped pcts
  and the precise pcts side-by-side for visual comparison.

All 34 risk checks pass; tsc, lint, build all green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Pack retune review: lottery-pack acknowledgment panel (tagged 1/5/10% packs)
entries.body:
Adds a prominent emerald explainer above the pack description in the
retune review card whenever a pack's name carries a leading hit-rate tag
<=10% (parsePackHitRate). Shows that the auto-retune recognized the
lottery pack, what it did differently (loosened the max-win cap to the
hit-rate-aware value via autoMaxWinCap's inverse-hit-rate scaling), the
concrete numbers (baseline 100x cap vs loosened cap vs top card kept),

entries.subject: Pack retune review: live EV/open chip in inline pool editor
entries.body:
Adds an EV/open metric chip to the editor's live AFTER preview, next to

existing computePackRisk result (PackRisk.ev) — no recompute, no extra

configured edge so the owner can see at a glance how far the current
pool's EV is from where it should land.

- ev < target → emerald (house healthy, less given back than budgeted)
- ev > target → rose (giving away more than budgeted)
- ev = target → neutral

Same PreviewTile primitive and AnimatedNumber currency format already used
by Max win — no new style. Grid widens to sm:grid-cols-5 so all five

entries.subject: Pack retune: band-aware error messages + no-win-band-card detection
entries.body:
shapeWeights infeasibility messages were vague (e.g. "Pool has no card
worth >= the $1.25 price") and didn't tell the operator WHICH band was
missing or what price range to add. Rewrites every HARD-limit detail +
suggestion to be band-aware and price-specific, and adds a NEW HARD
pre-check for the grail-only case where the math can't satisfy both the
target edge AND the target win-rate.

Changes (pure messaging, no algorithm/banding/threshold changes):

- no-win-cards: names the empty WIN+GRAIL bands and suggests a price
  range between $price and $5*price. New distinct sub-case when the
  maxWinCap pre-filter dropped cards — names the drop count, suggests
  either adding a card in the surviving range OR raising the cap.

- no-win-band-card (NEW kind): fires when pool has GRAIL cards but no
  WIN-band card in [price, 5*price), AND minEvAtWinRate (all win-mass
  on cheapest grail, rest on cheapest non-grail) exceeds evTarget. The
  message names the grail count, the missing WIN band ($price-$5*price),
  the target win-rate + edge, and suggests adding 1-2 small-win cards
  at concrete example prices (~2*price and ~4*price). If min EV is
  reachable, falls through unchanged to normal shaping.

- ev-out-of-range: names which side (too-low/too-high) and which band
  to add (DUST < 0.5*price, or WIN/GRAIL >= price).

- no-dust-cards: names the missing DUST band (< 0.5*price).

- degenerate-pool: names the example bands to add for variety.

- ev-unreachable-for-split, edge-unreachable: minor band-aware
  refinements only (focus per spec was on the four above).

Type system:

- Adds ShapeWeightsLimitKind union documenting the currently-emitted
  limit kinds. ShapeWeightsLimit.kind stays typed as string so
  consumers don't need an exhaustive switch (renderers just show
  detail + suggestion) and the set can be extended additively.

Tests (src/app/(admin)/packs/__checks__/risk.ts):

- 6g: expensive-grail-only pool (cheapest grail $200 at price $1.25,
  1% win-rate) -> no-win-band-card with suggestion mentioning
  $1.25-$6.25 WIN band.
- 6h: cheap-grail-only pool (the literal "1% 18 PLUS" scenario as
  described: cheapest grail $60.25, 1% win-rate) -> falls through to
  normal shaping (min EV reachable -> no-win-band-card does NOT fire).
- 6i: normal feasible pack still succeeds after the rewrite.
- 6j: cap-stripped pool down to zero usable cards -> empty-pool or
  no-win-cards naming the cap.
- 6k: cap-stripped WITH dust survivors -> distinct no-win-cards
  detail naming the cap-drop count and offering a raise-cap option.
- Full sweep still green: 11304 feasible / 5112 infeasible swept combos.

/pack-studio/retune (the new message on a real infeasible pack) is

entries.subject: Pack retune review: live "Total odds" chip in inline pool editor
entries.body:
The Bulk Re-tune review's pool editor has had an editable "Odds %" column
since the inline-edit landed, but nothing showed the running sum of the
per-card inputs. The owner just typed a pool that summed to 102% without
noticing.

Adds a live `OddsTotalChip` rendered TWICE inside the editor — once near
the top (between the price/add-card row and the live AFTER preview) and
once just above the Approve / Cancel buttons — so the total is visible
regardless of scroll position. The summation reuses `rows.map(r => r.odds)`
(the same view `approve` passes into `oddsToWeights`), so the chip and the
weights `applyPackEdit` writes can't drift.

House-style coloring:
  - exactly 100% (±0.005) → emerald + check icon
  - below 100%            → amber + info icon, "Under 100%"
  - above 100%            → rose, BOLD + larger, TriangleAlert,
                            "Over 100% — fix this before approving"

Format: `Total odds: NN.NN% / 100%` (2 decimals) with a one-liner explainer
("the auto-retune will renormalize, but your inputs should reflect what
you want"). Informational only — Approve stays enabled, owner can still
ship; this just makes a 102% input impossible to miss.

entries.subject: Pack retune: hit-rate-aware jackpot cap + portfolio feasibility floor
entries.body:
Stop the auto-optimizer from gutting low-hit-rate lottery packs. A "1%"/"5%"
pack needs a big jackpot to hold the house edge, but the plain 100x max-win cap
($125 on a $1.25 pack) stripped the $810 jackpot card -> pack went infeasible
or lost its jackpot.

CHANGE 1 (auto-targets.ts): autoMaxWinCap gains an optional hitRate param. The
price-relative multiplier now scales inversely with the intended hit-rate,
anchored at the default win-rate (0.20):
  scale = max(1, DEFAULT_TARGET_WIN_RATE / hitRate)  -> 1 at 20%, 4 at 5%, 20 at 1%
max(1, ...) guarantees a higher-than-default hit-rate is NEVER tightened below
100x; the globalCap clamp is preserved. autoRetuneTargets threads its parsed
intendedHitRate into the cap, so per-pack mode (planPackRetune via
resolveRetuneTargets) and doctor plan-all mode (already pass the pack name)
both keep lottery jackpots automatically. The builder's live edge-preview proxy
threads parsePackHitRate(name) too.

CHANGE 2 (portfolio.ts): derivePortfolioTargets' tighten loop now floors the
tightened cap at max(price, cheapest-win-card, hit-rate-aware jackpot floor) so
exposure-tightening can never (a) strip every win card -> infeasible, or
(b) gut a tagged lottery pack's jackpot. Untagged normal packs are unchanged
except they can no longer be tightened below their cheapest win card (pure
safety).

entries.subject: Pack Doctor snapshot: fix P2028 interactive-transaction timeout on prod
entries.body:
"Snapshot now" on /pack-studio/doctor crashed in production with
"An error occurred in the Server Components render". Captured the real
error from Vercel runtime logs (digest 3208459071, status 500):

  PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2028 — "A rollback cannot be executed
  on an expired transaction. The timeout for this transaction was 5000 ms,
  however 5257 ms passed since the start of the transaction."

Root cause: snapshotPackRisk upserted one pack_risk_scores row per active
cash pack inside a single Prisma transaction whose default interactive
timeout is 5000 ms. Against the remote ADMIN DB on Vercel serverless (cold
pool + network latency) the batch exceeds 5s and throws. It does not
reproduce on a local prod build because local DB latency is far lower —
hence environment-specific.

Fix:
- Convert the snapshot upsert batch from the array form
  $transaction([...]) (which does NOT accept timeout/maxWait — only the
  interactive callback form does) to $transaction(async (tx) => {...},
  { timeout: 120_000, maxWait: 15_000 }), keeping full atomicity. Pure
  scoring math is hoisted out of the transaction so the connection is held
  only for the writes.
- Add `export const maxDuration = 120` to the doctor route so the
  serverless function has matching budget and we never trade the Prisma
  timeout for a platform timeout.

Gated: tsc, lint, next build all green.

entries.subject: Pack risk shapeWeights: graceful relaxation of soft targets + structured limits
entries.body:
Make near-miss, modal-floor pin, and win-rate SOFT in the inverse weight
solver: when the pool genuinely cannot honour one, relax it down to the
achievable maximum (possibly 0) and proceed instead of hard-failing, recording
each give-up in a new ShapeWeightsSuccess.relaxations field. Edge stays HARD
(one-sided-up: edge >= targetEdge in every success).

Win-rate now relaxes against BOTH the mass budget AND EV feasibility: too much
mass on win/grail cards pins the minimum achievable EV above the edge target,
so the largest win mass admitting the edge is solved closed-form and the
win-rate relaxes to it.

Hard errors reserved for the truly impossible: no win/grail card, EV out of the
pool min/max value range, degenerate single-value pool (no spread), plus
backstops. Every error arm now carries a structured limit {kind, detail,
suggestion}. Union stays strictly disjoint (success: weights+relaxations;
error: error+limit).

Checks: assert a no-near-miss pool returns SUCCESS with a nearMiss relaxation
(applied 0) and edge >= target; a no-win pool returns the error arm with a
populated limit; an over-high win-rate relaxes to a feasible success; sweep
